expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against a fixed quota of low ratings and says why (it labels a fixed share of every team whatever its actual performance), while taking the CEO's underlying concern seriously.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "I'd not run the 10% quota with a fixed exit date. I'd run a calibrated review with a real support track instead. That still addresses underperformance..." Why: "In a team of six, 10% is 0.6 of a person, so someone is picked whether or not anyone is struggling." CEO line: "I want the same outcome you do: a higher standard and faster action on real underperformance."

expectations.text: The reply cites at least one real piece of evidence on forced or stack ranking, or on what drives performance differences between teams, with its source (for example Microsoft dropping stack ranking in 2013, simulation research on forced distribution, or research on managers' effect on teams).
expectations.evidence: "Microsoft, a well-known user, ended stack ranking in 2013 after years of criticism" with a Bloomberg link.

expectations.text: The reply flags that the works council must consent to the appraisal system in both countries (Netherlands: article 27(1)(g) WOR or its consent right on staff appraisal; Germany: §94 BetrVG appraisal principles), and that a plan starting from a ranking is weak ground for a later dismissal (the Dutch court expects timely notice, support and a real chance to improve; in Germany a low-performance dismissal usually needs a warning and proof).
expectations.evidence: "In the Netherlands, systems that can assess performance need council consent (art. 27(1)(l) WOR). In Germany... §87(1) no. 6 BetrVG gives similar co-determination, and §94 BetrVG covers assessment principles"; NL dismissal "goes to the cantonal court. It expects the employee to have been told in good time, supported and given a real chance to improve (art. 7:669(3)(d) BW). A rank or quota is no evidence"; DE "normally needs documented shortfalls and prior warnings." The substance passes, but the Dutch article is wrong: appraisal is 27(1)(g), (l) covers monitoring facilities.

expectations.text: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
expectations.evidence: Document: one-page standards per role family; calibration "Check that ratings are consistent across teams and free of bias... The expected spread is a sanity check, never a target"; support plan with coaching, training, weekly check-ins, first formal review at 60 days, then "plan continues with new dates", redeploy, or HR and counsel decide.

expectations.text: The reply includes a check of ratings by group (such as gender, age, part-time or people on leave) before ratings are used for pay, plans or exits.
expectations.evidence: No clear by-group check before ratings are used. Calibration says only "free of bias". The group breakdown sits in 'Measures we review' and covers "Share of 'needs support' ratings reversed or changed in calibration, and the pattern by team, gender, age, location and part-time status". That is a programme metric on reversals, with no step placing it before plans or exits.

expectations.text: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
expectations.evidence: "Raise it privately first, before any wider forum. For example: 'I want the same outcome you do...'" Document Part 2 is a manager briefing (asks, not-asks, biases, conversation, support plan basics).

overall_quality.evidence: Concise, sound and usable, with a good private CEO line and a clear reversible/irreversible split, but thin on evidence, weak on group-level fairness checks, and it cites the wrong WOR article.

factual_errors.evidence: Cites art. 27(1)(l) WOR (consent for facilities that monitor attendance, behaviour or performance) as the consent right for the appraisal system; the staff-appraisal consent right is art. 27(1)(g). Trivial: 'mandatory above 50 employees' (it is from 50).

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill or reference files.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt is a proposed policy, not a bad outcome.

best_insight.value: Offer the CEO two things that meet his intent: leaders go through the same calibration first, and a quarterly report on plans and how they end; and split what can start now (standards, works council briefing, manager training) from what must wait (any distribution, exit date or announcement).
best_insight.evidence: 'How to take it to the CEO' and 'What I'd start now'.

suggestions.assertion: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
suggestions.reason: Several samples swap the quota for a company- or function-level 'expected range' (e.g. 10-17% at the bottom) drawn from an unsourced framework. Add a check that no expected or target share is introduced, or that any reference range is sourced and never used to move a rating.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
suggestions.reason: Nearly any CEO talking point passes. Consider requiring that the conversation comes before ExCo, managers or works councils and that it tests what 'it worked at his last company' meant (measure, period, legal setting).

No assertion checks that the reply separates a possible cost or headcount goal from performance management (restructuring route, collective-dismissal rules if exits are driven by a fixed number). The strongest samples do this.
No assertion checks the Dutch route for a performance dismissal (cantonal court, not UWV); at least one sample gets this wrong and still passes assertion 3.

suggestions.assertion: The reply includes a check of ratings by group (such as gender, age, part-time or people on leave) before ratings are used for pay, plans or exits.
suggestions.reason: This works well: it separates samples that only say 'free of bias' or review patterns after plans from those that check group patterns before ratings are final.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertion 5 discriminates well here; assertion 3 passes on substance despite a wrong article number. Consider requiring the right legal basis.
